dossiers.counterevidence: Magnitude and attribution can weaken or reverse across places and periods; the edge is not deterministic.

dossiers.mechanism: Large or unstable staple-price changes reduce purchasing power and planning security for households with limited income or food reserves.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Households exposed to the affected staple market, especially low-income and import-dependent populations.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Weeks to months, potentially longer under sustained shocks.
dossiers.counterevidence: Some producers benefit from higher prices and safety nets can mitigate household food-access effects.

indicator.metric_name: Staple-food price variance and affordability relative to household income
indicator.unit: local currency per kilogram, percent change, and percent of household expenditure
indicator.geography: country, market, or subnational price series
indicator.transformation: Use a defined staple basket, inflation-adjusted prices, comparable market coverage, and household-expenditure context; retain supply and policy shock annotations.
indicator.uncertainty: Prices reflect currency changes, market selection, subsidies, reporting gaps, and quality differences as well as physical supply.
indicator.threshold_provenance: Country-specific historical volatility and affordability baseline.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not publish a price-volatility trend from sparse or incomparable market observations.

source_locators.locator: FAO: volatility, household exposure, and food-security implications
World Bank: transport costs, food prices, and food security

dossiers.mechanism: Persistent loss of soil, vegetation, water availability, and ecosystem services can reduce or destabilize crop and livestock production and erode household capacity to absorb climate and market shocks.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Named dryland food system and exposed population with production, access, and livelihood indicators stated separately.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Growing-season losses through chronic multi-year livelihood effects.
dossiers.counterevidence: Land condition is only one component of food security, and imports, income, irrigation, technology, and social protection can buffer local production losses.

indicator.unit: hectares and percent of fixed dryland baseline, with land productivity, vegetation cover, soil condition, and carbon-stock components reported separately
indicator.geography: named dryland assessment unit, watershed, rangeland, agricultural district, or country reporting boundary
indicator.cadence: annual land-condition update with multi-year trend review
indicator.transformation: Retain the dryland definition, fixed spatial baseline, land-cover class, productivity trajectory, soil and vegetation observations, climate covariates, management history, degradation criterion, restoration activity, and uncertainty.
indicator.uncertainty: Climate variability, sensor changes, land-cover classification, grazing intensity, crop cycles, soil sampling, choice of baseline, and older global assessment methods can change apparent extent and direction.
indicator.threshold_provenance: Use the UNCCD reporting framework or a named regional assessment; no single productivity decline or drought year establishes persistent degradation.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not infer persistent degradation from aridity, drought, bare soil, or a one-year vegetation anomaly without a fixed boundary and multi-indicator evidence.

source_locators.locator: IPCC assesses combined climate and degradation pressures as contributing to food insecurity and reduced ecosystem services, with strong context dependence.
UNCCD lists lack of food security among the economic, social, and environmental problems aggravated by desertification.

dossiers.mechanism: Excess nutrient and organic-carbon runoff can alter coastal water chemistry, promote blooms, and increase reef stress that compounds thermal bleaching susceptibility and recovery limits.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Named reef, ecoregion, or satellite grid cell.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Days to a bleaching season, with field validation.
dossiers.counterevidence: Nutrient enrichment is not a bleaching diagnosis; it must be distinguished from thermal exposure, sedimentation, and disease through water-quality and reef observations.

indicator.metric_name: Coral bleaching severity and thermal stress
indicator.unit: percent coral colonies bleached, bleaching alert level, or degree-heating-weeks
indicator.geography: named reef, ecoregion, or satellite grid cell
indicator.cadence: daily thermal monitoring plus seasonal field validation
indicator.transformation: Retain coral taxon, survey method, depth, heat-stress metric, exposure duration, and local water-quality context.
indicator.uncertainty: Satellite heat-stress products require field validation; susceptibility differs by species, acclimation, depth, and local stressors.
indicator.threshold_provenance: NOAA Coral Reef Watch Degree Heating Week and Bleaching HotSpot products.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not infer bleaching from a warm anomaly alone without duration, reef location, and field or validated heat-stress context.

source_locators.locator: NOAA: excess nutrient and organic-carbon runoff can drive blooms and local coastal acidification.
NOAA AOML identifies water-quality stressors alongside heat, disease, hypoxia, and acidification as reef threats.

dossiers.mechanism: Excess nutrient delivery can increase algal production; respiration during decomposition then consumes bottom-water oxygen faster than it is replenished.
dossiers.geographic_scope: River-influenced continental shelves with nutrient-load, productivity, and bottom-water oxygen observations.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Runoff and bloom events through seasonal hypoxic-area development.
dossiers.counterevidence: Elevated nutrients do not establish low oxygen without biological production, respiration, and limited ventilation.

indicator.unit: milligrams per liter or milliliters per liter dissolved oxygen with hypoxic area, water-column thickness, duration, depth, threshold and global site inventory reported separately
indicator.geography: named continental-shelf survey grid, transect, bottom-water station network, model domain, or declared global assessment boundary
indicator.cadence: continuous station observations or repeated seasonal surveys with annual synthesis and global assessment reviews
indicator.transformation: Retain depth, distance above seabed, instrument and calibration, temperature, salinity, density structure, threshold, survey coverage, interpolation method, and whether the record is observed or modeled.
indicator.uncertainty: Sparse transects, sensor drift, short-lived mixing, tidal and upwelling variability, threshold choice, and interpolation across unobserved shelf water affect area and duration estimates.
indicator.threshold_provenance: Use the named monitoring program threshold, such as 2 milligrams per liter or 1.4 milliliters per liter, without treating thresholds from different programs as interchangeable.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not infer shelf-wide hypoxia from one low-oxygen station, substitute a global oxygen trend for local observations, or merge measurements that use incompatible depth and threshold definitions.

source_locators.locator: NOAA identifies excess nutrients, algal production, organic carbon, and decomposition as a major continental-shelf oxygen-depletion pathway.
EPA links eutrophication and decomposition of algal organic matter to documented coastal low-oxygen conditions.

dossiers.mechanism: Nutrient-rich, turbid coastal water can increase production and create conditions favorable to some bloom-forming taxa and their prey.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Named coastal water body with taxon-resolved abundance, nutrients, oxygen, and circulation.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Seasonal loading through bloom development.
dossiers.counterevidence: Nutrient enrichment does not favor every jellyfish species or create a bloom by itself.

indicator.metric_name: Jellyfish bloom frequency, biomass, and duration
indicator.unit: individuals per cubic metre, biomass, occupied area, event duration, and recurrence by taxon and method
indicator.geography: named coastal water body, taxon, life stage, depth, survey platform, season, and baseline
indicator.cadence: seasonal or annual observation with multi-year trend review
indicator.transformation: Retain medusa and polyp stages, taxon, sampling effort, artificial substrate, temperature, salinity, oxygen, nutrients, prey, predators, fishing, currents, and uncertainty.
indicator.uncertainty: Patchiness, life-cycle stage, currents, observation effort, taxonomic ambiguity, and episodic recruitment complicate trend inference.
indicator.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative or primary study method and a declared taxonomic, spatial, temporal, and baseline boundary; no universal collapse threshold is implied.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not infer a regional increase from beach strandings, intake fouling, or one survey without effort-adjusted abundance and a fixed baseline.

source_locators.locator: NOAA identifies murky nutrient-rich water as favorable in the studied coastal setting.
NOAA synthesis records eutrophication among multiple, interacting bloom drivers.

dossiers.mechanism: Excess nutrients and associated oxygen, algal, ammonia, or sediment changes can impair sensitive life stages where exposure reaches harmful levels.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Named river reach with taxon, water-quality, sediment, and comparable population observations.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Seasonal exposure through years of recruitment and survival response.
dossiers.counterevidence: Nutrient concentration alone does not identify the causal toxic or habitat pathway.

indicator.unit: density, catch per unit effort, occupancy, species richness, survival, recruitment, and size structure by survey method
indicator.geography: named river reach, mussel taxon and host context, habitat, survey design, and assessment period
indicator.cadence: seasonal or annual observation with multi-year trend review
indicator.transformation: Retain taxon, life stage, host fish, detection and effort, flow, temperature, substrate, sediment, barriers, contaminants, disease, non-native species, drought, and uncertainty.
indicator.uncertainty: Imperfect detection, patchy beds, long life spans, episodic recruitment, host dynamics, flow, pollution, and unexplained mass mortality affect trends.
indicator.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative or primary study method and a declared taxonomic, spatial, temporal, and baseline boundary; no universal collapse threshold is implied.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not infer a cause from absence or one survey, and do not generalize a site-specific decline across taxa or basins.

dossiers.mechanism: Loss of vegetated seabed removes living carbon uptake and can expose carbon-rich sediment to erosion and remineralization.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Mapped seagrass beds with repeat habitat and sediment-carbon observations.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Seasonal damage through multi-year stock change.
dossiers.counterevidence: Canopy decline does not prove stored carbon was released without sediment and disturbance measurements.

indicator.metric_name: Coastal blue-carbon habitat area and carbon-stock loss
indicator.unit: hectares lost and tonnes carbon or carbon dioxide equivalent released or sequestration capacity lost
indicator.geography: global assessment or named salt-marsh, mangrove, or seagrass assessment area
indicator.cadence: major global assessment or annual to multi-year inventory
indicator.transformation: Retain habitat class, mapped area, soil depth, carbon-stock method, disturbance type, baseline year, and whether release or avoided sequestration is estimated.
indicator.uncertainty: Below-ground stocks, erosion fate, remineralization, mapping resolution, and counterfactual sequestration vary by habitat and method.
indicator.threshold_provenance: Habitat-specific inventory method or IPCC wetlands accounting boundary.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not convert habitat area directly to emissions without habitat-specific stock and disturbance factors.

source_locators.locator: NOAA identifies seagrass beds as coastal carbon stores and explains that damage removes uptake and can release stored carbon.
NOAA white paper defines seagrass as a blue-carbon ecosystem and provides inventory context.

dossiers.mechanism: Buildings, roads, and other dense surfaces absorb energy and release it slowly after sunset while limited vegetation reduces evaporative cooling.
dossiers.geographic_scope: Named urban area with paired canopy-layer air-temperature observations and a defined reference area.
dossiers.temporal_scope: Evening through predawn, summarized by season and heat event.
dossiers.counterevidence: A warm night is not evidence of a local urban contrast without a comparable reference observation.

indicator.unit: degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit with urban and reference sites, height, local time, and averaging window stated
indicator.geography: named city and matched rural or intra-urban reference network
indicator.cadence: hourly observations with nightly, seasonal, and heat-event summaries
indicator.transformation: Pair comparable canopy-layer air-temperature observations; retain station siting, height, land cover, local time, weather, season, and reference definition. Surface temperature remains separate.
indicator.uncertainty: Station siting, urban morphology, wind, cloud cover, humidity, advection, season, and the rural reference affect the measured difference.
indicator.threshold_provenance: City-specific paired observations and EPA heat-island measurement guidance; no universal nighttime threshold is implied.
indicator.failure_behavior: Do not mix satellite surface temperature with near-surface air temperature or infer a citywide value from one unpaired station.

source_locators.locator: EPA reports systematically higher nighttime urban temperatures and identifies heat absorption and re-emission by built surfaces.
EPA provides a nighttime atmospheric heat-island measurement framework using paired air-temperature observations.
